chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Abu Maryam from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

The one who takes an oath of abstention (muda'ib) is paused for four months; if he wishes, he may keep her in a good manner or release her with kindness; if he determines divorce, then it is one revocable divorce, and he has the right to take her back.

key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَةِ الْأَشْهُرِ: The four-month period granted for decision
key_terms.الْمُؤْلِي: The husband who takes an oath of abstention from conjugal relations
key_terms.رَجْعَتِهَا: His right to take her back (revocation of divorce)
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One (referring to a single revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and waiting period for a husband who takes an oath of abstention (Ila) from his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural outcome of *ila* (oath of abstention) by specifying that the four-month period concludes with a single revocable divorce (*talaq raj'i*), granting the husband the right of return without a new marriage contract. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling emphasizes the transition from a state of suspended intimacy to a formalized separation, reflecting the Quranic balance between patience and decisive action. The narration underscores the husband's continued authority (*amlik*) over the reconciliation process during the *iddah* period following this specific type of divorce.
